phase3_findings.description: The updated block comment enumerates 'absent' and 'non-string' login states alongside the reachable 'blank'/'whitespace-only' ones, but the COMMITS projection defaults logins with `// ""` so absent/non-string are unreachable here; the type guards are defensive-only. Not a falsehood (comment does not claim they occur), but may mislead a maintainer.

Comment 'The "last bot commit" anchor (below) is unchanged' is imprecise: the anchor selection was changed to route through the new type-guarded ends_bot() (a null-safety change). Behavior is identical for the always-string real inputs, but a literal reader sees the anchor lines changed. Consider 'behaves the same for string logins'.

The modified test comment block is ~7 physical lines and largely design rationale/provenance; under the prevention-only comment standard (test files in scope) only the 'never a transcribed copy -- a copy keeps passing after the shipped filter drifts' clause is prevention-bearing. Trimmable.

No fixture supplies a non-string login (e.g. numeric); the type == "string" guard branch is unpinned. A one-row numeric-login-tail -> 0 fixture would pin it. (Independently verified: numeric login currently yields 0, correct.)
No fixture for the zero-bot-anchor / empty-commits path (`if ($bot_indices | length) == 0`). Low risk (branch unchanged by PR) but cheap to close.

POSTBOT_SHAS has a single fixture vs 7 for the count block; a divergence introduced only in the SHA block would rely on the coupling holding. Adding null/whitespace variants to _pbs keeps mirror protection symmetric.
